parts.label: Part 2
parts.article:
This week, our slot is A Life in the Day of Joan Gilbert, local organiser for Riding for the Disabled. Joan, would you like to tell us about this?
Well, I always have the very best intentions of starting the day at 05:30 to give the horses a really good muck out, but reality intervenes and I finally wake at about 06:30. That probably still sounds very early to you. But for a farm worker, which is what my son is at the moment, that's cutting things pretty fine.
Once I've managed to get him safely on his way at about 07:00, I can start turning my attention to the other important tasks of the day. For about five years, we've been taking overseas students from the International Centre at our local college, and I have to give them a proper breakfast. Most of our students used to be from the Middle East, but they're no longer coming. So we tend to have Malaysian girls, and they like to have a cooked breakfast much more than any Europeans we've had, including me. And I don't have anything these days. After cooking, I finally get round to the poor horses.
It's only after this that I can start thinking about what I regard as my most important task — work for Riding for the Disabled. I've been involved with this organisation on and off for over 20 years, but I've only recently taken on the job of chairperson. Most of the work seems more secretarial, but that's how charities get organised. In our immediate district, we have had as many as 30 riders, but currently we've only got 22. The number of helpers who have volunteered is actually 40, but we can rely on 25 to come regularly to help in the different groups. We now have four separate groups which cater for disabled children and adults from six to 40 years old.
As I say, I feel that although I no longer have any proper full-time paid employment, I do have a full and busy life. I'm a housewife, which I don't mind because I don't really object to doing things like washing and cooking. Then there's my own horses, which I adore — even the revolting stuff like cleaning out the stables. The official RDA stuff is a mixed bag, really. I don't have major problems with all the letter writing and correspondence which it entails, but like lots of shy people, I find the fundraising horrendous. Other regular RDA duties, such as ringing round the riders to fix times, etc., are among the pleasantest aspects of the work. After all, that's why I'm involved with charity work — the contact with people. My working day ends with the least enjoyable job of all, sorting the accounts.
I got involved with RDA because I've always loved horses and I can see disabled people gaining so much. I know all the medical evidence that shows that it does wonders for muscle building and so on, which is important. But from talking to the riders, they say it is the confidence they gain, and also the opportunity to be part of a new and exciting environment, which gives them the greatest benefit.
In terms of the RDA organisation itself, I feel it works very well, but we're always striving to make it better. I wish, for example, our helpers and the organisers in the various centres could really rationalise the fundraising efforts, which are sometimes very inefficient. And it also saddens me how unaware some of the stables can be about the difficulties faced by people who are disabled. Anyway, I feel very privileged to work with our riders and to see such tangible benefits. It sends me to sleep with a feeling that, though the day has been hard, it has been worthwhile.

analyses.content: Joan 说她虽然总想（intentions）在 5:30 起床，但现实是她最终醒来（finally wake）是在 6:30。
Well, I always have the very best intentions of starting the day at 05:30 to give the horses a really good muck out, but reality intervenes and I finally wake at about 06:30.
你可能听到 5:30 就激动地选了 A，但那是她“打算”的时间，不是实际发生的时间。

questions.question: Joan's first task of the day is to

analyses.content: Once I've managed to get him safely on his way at about 07:00, I can start turning my attention to the other important tasks of the day.
你可能觉得既然是马场就要先照顾马（选 A），但录音明确说她是做完早饭后才腾出手照顾“可怜的马（poor horses）”的。
录音中提到，只有当她在 7:00 把儿子送走（get him safely on his way）之后，才能开始关注其他任务，说明送儿子是第一件事。

groups.contentHtml: Joan's official title in Riding for the Disabled (RDA) is chairperson. In her local district there at present twenty two riders and helpers on the volunteer list, out of whom come regularly.

analyses.content: In our immediate district, we have had as many as 30 riders, but currently we've only got 22. The number of helpers who have volunteered is actually 40...
注意区分干扰数字，30 是过去的骑手人数，22 是现在的骑手人数，不要填错行。
录音直接说志愿者名单上的帮忙者数量（helpers who have volunteered）实际上是 40 人。
The number of helpers who have volunteered is actually 40, but we can rely on 25 to come regularly to help in the different groups.
听到 "regularly"（定期）这个词时，要立刻抓取紧随其后的数字 25。
虽然总数有 40 人，但 Joan 强调他们能“依赖（rely on）”也就是定期来帮忙的人数是 25 人。

analyses.content: I don't have major problems with all the letter writing and correspondence which it entails...
不要主观以为文书工作很枯燥就选 C，要听她说 "don't have major problems" 这种中立的态度。
Joan 说她对于写信和通信（correspondence）并没有太大的问题（don't have major problems），对应选项 B 的“不介意”。
Joan 形容筹款（fundraising）这件事是 "horrendous"（可怕的/糟糕的），显然她非常讨厌。
...but like lots of shy people, I find the fundraising horrendous.
Horrendous 是个强烈的贬义词，听到这个词就应该直接对应 Hate。
Other regular RDA duties, such as ringing round the riders to fix times, etc., are among the pleasantest aspects of the work.
听到 "pleasantest" 这种最高级褒义词，直接选表达最积极的选项。
Joan 说给骑手打电话（ringing round）是工作中“最愉快（pleasantest）”的部分之一，对应选项 A 的“真正喜欢”。
My working day ends with the least enjoyable job of all, sorting the accounts.
听到 "Least enjoyable"（最不享受）就等同于 hate，不要犹豫。
Joan 说整理账目（sorting the accounts）是所有工作中“最不享受（least enjoyable）”的，即讨厌。

Joan 希望能使筹款工作（fundraising efforts）更合理化，因为现在“效率非常低（very inefficient）”，意味着需要变得更有效（more effective）。

analyses.content: I wish, for example, our helpers and the organisers in the various centres could really rationalise the fundraising efforts, which are sometimes very inefficient. And it also saddens me how unaware some of the stables can be about the difficulties faced by people who are disabled.
你可能听到 training 就想选 A，但录音没有提到需要特殊培训，而是强调 awareness（意识）。
Joan 提到让她难过的是，一些马厩对残疾人面临的“困难（difficulties）”非常“不了解（unaware）”，这意味着需要提高这种认识。
